title: Bellingham is one of the best but Zidane comparisons unnecessary – Mourinho
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutBellingham is one of the best but Zidane comparisons unnecessary – MourinhoShareJude Bellingham has been compared to Zinedine Zidane, one of Real Madrid's greatest-ever players, after his stunning goal versus PSV.Jose Mourinho was unwilling to engage in comparisons between Jude Bellingham and Zinedine Zidane, though he feels the England international has already proven himself as one of the best players of his generation.

Bellingham scored a sensational goal as Madrid routed PSV 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday, taking two touches without letting the ball bounce, then finding the net with an outside-of-the-boot volley from distance.
The goal inevitably drew comparisons to another much-feted Madrid playmaker in Zidane, who scored a famous volley in Los Blancos' 2002 Champions League final win over Bayer Leverkusen.
But when asked about that likeness on Friday, ahead of Madrid hosting Alaves in LaLiga on Saturday, Mourinho said: "I don't like comparing players from different generations.
"Zidane was one of the best players in the world in his generation, and Jude already is [one of the best] in his own generation. I don't like comparisons."

Mourinho was also asked how he viewed the competition for places in his attack, after Bellingham and Brahim Diaz – who put pen to paper on a new five-year contract on Friday – started Tuesday's game on the bench.
There has been much debate over whether Vinicius Junior and Yan Diomande can play together, but they played on opposite flanks against PSV to great effect.
Madrid have an 81.8% win rate with Vinicius in their starting XI this season (nine wins, two defeats) but have won all six of their matches when the Brazilian has not started.
However, Mourinho pushed back on the framing of that debate, saying: "Vinicius and Diomande are not in competition. Here, we are all together and want the same goal.
"It's something that has taken a lot of work to build, and it has one of the least valued yet most important things in the last five months; making this group work as a team.
"Now that we have a level of stability, it seems your temptation is to create these kinds of circumstances. If someone scores, it's a Real Madrid goal. That's what we want."

Alaves, who are ninth in the table, beat Deportivo A Coruna 3-1 last Saturday, ending their worst winless run in LaLiga (eight games – D3 L5) since February 2022 (11 games – D4 L7). However, they have not achieved two consecutive wins in the competition since September 2026.
Who else but Bellingham? He scored his 17th Champions League goal – and his first as a substitute – in remarkable fashion on Tuesday.

Bellingham is one of three Madrid players in double figures for combined goal involvements in all competitions this season, having scored seven and teed up four (11, also Kylian Mbappe with 24 and Arda Guler with 12).
Against Deportivo last time out, Boye became the first Alaves player to score a goal, register an assist and miss a penalty in a single LaLiga game this century.
Will Saturday's game be just as eventful for the visitors' leading scorer, who has six goals to his name in LaLiga this season?
Real Madrid have won 18 of their 20 home games against Alaves in LaLiga, losing the other two.
It is their highest number of home encounters without a single draw against the same opponent in their history in the competition.
Overall, Alaves have lost their last nine matches against Madrid in LaLiga – they could lose 10 straight games against a single opponent for the first time in their top-flight history.
Madrid are strong favourites, having won their last nine home matches in LaLiga, including all six under Mourinho last season.
